# Contacts

An address book where the **key**, not the name or photo, is the thing being verified — every
contact card shows a real trust status, not just a name and an avatar. Contacts are `kind =
contact` MOTEs (JSContact-shaped), synced the same way as mail, chat, and calendar.

![Contacts — cards with key-verification status](assets/screens/contacts-dark.png)

## Finding and organizing contacts

Open **Contacts** from the left rail. The list is searchable, filterable, and sortable (by name,
recently added, or verification status), and each card shows org/title/phone, tag-based
organization, and membership in any addressable [groups](#groups) you share.

## Reading the verification status

Every card shows one of three states front and center:

- **Verified** — you've compared this contact's [safety number](#identity#safety-numbers)
  out-of-band and confirmed the key. Look for the ✓ badge.
- **TOFU-pinned** — trust-on-first-use: you've exchanged messages, so a key is pinned, but you
  haven't independently verified it yet.
- **Legacy** — the contact has no DMTAP key at all; you only have a legacy (SMTP) address for
  them, reached through the [gateway](#self-hosting).

**To verify a TOFU-pinned contact:** open their card, find the safety-number affordance, and
compare it against theirs out-of-band — see [Identity](#identity#safety-numbers-verifying-a-contacts-key)
for the full steps. This is the one thing that closes the gap trust-on-first-use leaves open: a
look-alike key substituted before either side has verified anything. Putting that status directly
on the card, rather than burying it in a details screen, is deliberate.

## Avatars

Gradient avatars, an opt-in Gravatar-style hash avatar, or a key-derived identicon — see
[Identity](#identity#avatars-and-profile) for the full ladder; the same standard applies to your
own profile and to how a contact's picture is rendered here.

## Jumping into other apps from a contact

Quick actions on a card jump straight into [Mail](#mail) (compose to them), [Chat](#chat), or
a prefilled meeting invite in [Calendar](#calendar) — contacts are the shared address book every
other module reads from, not a silo. Import/export affordances are available from the list header.

## What's real vs. simulated today

Contact creation, tagging, filtering, import/export, and the verification-status computation
(a real deterministic safety-number derivation) are real code. As with every other module in this
reference client, the address book itself is seeded demo data and there is no real directory sync
yet — a production client resolves and pins contacts against the real naming/key-transparency
stack in [`crates/dmtap-naming`](https://github.com/vul-os/envoir/blob/main/crates/dmtap-naming). See [Roadmap](#roadmap) for the
project-wide real-vs-simulated line.
